name: agentavow-trust
description: Checks your MCP servers and packages with AgentAvow before Codex uses them. When a session starts it checks the servers in ~/.codex/config.toml and a trusted project's .codex/config.toml. When Codex runs codex mcp add, or installs a package by name with npm, pnpm, yarn, bun, pip, uv, pipx or poetry, it checks that exact version first: Do not connect stops the step and says why, Review before you connect is a one-line note, and Safe to connect stays silent. Every answer has its reason and a signed 0-100 trust score you can verify offline. Also bundles the AgentAvow connector and the scan-before-connect skill. The hooks run only while you trust them (/hooks). Fail-open. What leaves your machine: the server URL or package name being checked, and a random install ID used only to count active installs, also sent once a day with the plugin version and app type (turn it off with AGENTAVOW_ANON_ID=off).

interface.shortDescription: Is this tool safe to connect?
interface.longDescription: AgentAvow checks an MCP server or package before Codex adds or installs it, and answers in plain words: Safe to connect, Review before you connect, or Do not connect, with the reason. Underneath are a 0-100 trust score, backed by a signed attestation anyone can verify offline, and an adoption score. In the Codex CLI and desktop app the plugin's hooks check your servers at session start and stop a codex mcp add or package install that reads Do not connect. The bundled connector and skill answer when you ask about a tool. No account and no sign-in.
defaultPrompt: Is the npm package chalk safe to install?
